source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Understand the components: Identify the various components of the brake system that were tested—brake pads, rotors, calipers, brake lines, master cylinder, brake fluid, ABS (anti-lock brake system), and parking brake.

3. Record the date and time: Note down the exact date and time the test was conducted. This helps track when issues were identified, which may be crucial for warranty claims or recalling the vehicle's repair history.

4. List the vehicle specifics: Include make, model, year, VIN (Vehicle Identification Number), current mileage, and license plate number. This ensures the right vehicle record is updated.

5. Document the test procedure: Write down which brake test was performed—this could include a visual inspection, a pressure test, a road test, or a computer-diagnostic test using an OBD (On-Board Diagnostics) scanner.

6. Detail failed components: For each failed component, provide a detailed description.
